svg.title: Layered Logic Mirror — Find Mirror / Multi-Mirror Picker screen wireframe
svg.desc: Lo-fi wireframe of the Controls page connection panel in the Layered Logic Mirror app, showing the multi-mirror picker that appears when more than one mirror is discovered via mDNS. Shows the resting state (Mirror URL input, Find mirror + SoftAP action buttons, 3-row picker with name + IP + id rows, Connect/Disconnect controls with connection state pill) with 6 numbered callouts pairing each design decision to its source rationale. A 4-thumbnail strip below documents the initial-empty, searching, single-mirror-auto-selected, and no-mirror-found-with-VPN-hint alternate states. Phone proportions match Pixel 9 (360x800 dp, 9:20 ratio). Brand indigo (#3214FF) marks the active row and primary affordances.
svg.text: Layered Logic Mirror · App/v1 · Mobile (React Native, Pixel 9)
"Find mirror" runs a 2.5s mDNS query via Android's NsdManager,
not a subnet sweep. Replaces a 254-host parallel-fetch scan that
drowned in OkHttp's 64-concurrent-request cap. mDNS is also
subnet-tolerant — phone and mirror can be on different /24s.
Exactly one mirror found → URL fills automatically, picker doesn't
render. Showing a single-row picker would force the user to tap an
otherwise-redundant button. The picker is a disambiguation surface,
not a confirmation surface — it only appears when needed.
Same principle, opposite case: zero results show an error toast,
one auto-selects, two-or-more surfaces the picker. The label
explicitly says how many were found so the user knows whether to
expect their other mirrors in the list.
Row label = name; sub = IP · id
Display name (user-set in Settings) takes the top line in 14pt;
sub-row in mono shows IP + id (the 6-hex MAC suffix). If the
mirror has no name set, the row's primary label falls back to the
id — never blank. id stays visible in the sub line either way for
when two mirrors get the same nickname.
Tapping SoftAP sets URL to http://192.168.4.1/ — the mirror's
setup-mode IP. Lets the user re-provision a misconfigured mirror
without typing the address. Goes active (filled style) when the
No auto-connect on URL change — gives the user a deterministic
trigger. Pill on the right shows live WS state (idle / connecting
/ open / closing) so users debugging a connection can see exactly
Pre-scan default, in-flight searching, single-result auto-fill, and no-result error with VPN-disable hint.
